items.observation: The broad pale central bed has fixed marks. Along its right interior margin a darker rough narrow band repeatedly changes lobes and knots; an outer white-water strip is distinct. The fixed central area alone cannot support N for the whole frame.
items.conclusion: Retain the existing P for now; no definite N counterexample in this sampled minute. Do not claim every pale part is flowing.

items.observation: Central bed stones remain fixed; the right narrow dark band changes local rough patches, separate from bright edge water.
items.conclusion: Same scoped conclusion; no new T is established. No exact end-of-event boundary follows from these samples.

items.observation: A narrow pale-brown band occupies the steep lower channel; its local contour changes, while foreground gravel is fixed. Fog and distance prevent a reliable reading of transported material.
items.conclusion: Fluid motion is visible, but its type is not resolved by these audit images. Do not use thinness to change P to N or T. Flag current P supervision for explicit uncertainty adjudication rather than calling this a confirmed error.

items.observation: A brighter, locally broader band and changing lobes are visible in the lower bend. The upper band remains distant.
items.conclusion: Widening alone is not a global P threshold; no physically precise onset or forced T is supported. Compare with earlier type uncertainty.

items.observation: Night images show fixed central deposit ridges and a changing left shiny strip. At325.29 there is a bright exposure flash; other frames return to the darker view.
items.conclusion: Do not mistake flash-induced differences for motion. These samples do not establish whether the left strip is ordinary water or target slurry; no forced N/P/T decision from brightness alone.

limits: These are specified local intervals, not continuous full-video viewing or a geological concentration measurement.
